title: Lane Merge
statement: A swim meet records finishing times per lane, and each lane's list is already sorted from fastest to slowest (smallest to largest). Merge all lanes into one list of every time, sorted from smallest to largest. Some lanes may be empty.
constraints: Each lane is sorted in non-decreasing order
At most 10000 times in total, each between -1000000 and 1000000

hints.content: Concatenating everything and sorting works but ignores the per-lane order.
The next smallest time overall is always the front of some lane.
With k lanes, scanning every front costs k per output value.
Keep the current front of each lane in a min-heap, keyed by value.
Pop the smallest, output it, and push the next time from the same lane. JavaScript has no built-in heap, so write a small one.

testCases.explanation: Many lanes that each contribute one value per block of 200.

solutions.title: Flatten and sort
solutions.intuition: The merged list is just every value in sorted order.
solutions.approach: Flatten all lanes into one array and sort numerically.
solutions.interviewExplanation: Flattening and sorting is correct in O(N log N). It ignores that each lane is already sorted, which the heap approach exploits to get O(N log k).

solutions.title: Min-heap of lane fronts
solutions.intuition: Only the k lane fronts are candidates for the next output, and a heap finds the smallest in O(log k).
solutions.approach: Push [value, lane, index] for each non-empty lane. Repeatedly pop the minimum, output its value, and push the next element of that lane if any.
solutions.spaceComplexity: O(k) for the heap, plus the output
commonMistakes: Pushing every value into the heap at the start, which is O(N log N) and loses the benefit.
Forgetting to skip empty lanes when seeding the heap.
solutions.interviewExplanation: The next output is always one of the k lane fronts, so I keep just those in a min-heap. Each pop outputs a value and pushes its lane's successor, so scanning the k lanes and processing N values costs O(k + N log(k + 1)) total with O(k) heap space. The initial scan still costs O(k) when all lanes are empty. Merging lanes pairwise in rounds gives the same bound without a heap.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.content: The heap starts with fronts 1 (lane 0), 1 (lane 1) and 2 (lane 2).

steps.title: Step 2
steps.content: Pop 1 (lane 0) and push 4. Pop 1 (lane 1) and push 3. Pop 2 and push 6. Pop 3 and push 4…
